prospect.name: Samuel Mathew
prospect.location: New Jersey, USA (born in India, in the US over 20 years)
prospect.occupation: MRI technologist; a mix of sitting and standing, with two long shift days a week
prospect.family_status: Married; travels frequently with his wife; has adult children; mother-in-law lives with them and recently had a stroke; no grandchildren yet
prospect.training_background: Lifelong on-off pattern of training and dieting — keto, carnivore and others — never sustained, never gained muscle. Nine consecutive weeks of home-gym strength training at the time of the call: elliptical warm-up, squats, chest press, seated row, deadlift on Tuesdays; split squats, incline press, lat pull-down, hamstring curl on Fridays; a lighter session plus farmer's carries on Saturdays. Walks 7,000-8,000 steps daily. Owns a 30 lb kettlebell and has only ever done swings; ordered an adjustable kettlebell the day of the call.
prospect.medical: Currently three weeks into tirzepatide, a GLP-1 agonist, and down nine pounds; states he must weight train and eat high protein on it to avoid muscle loss. Long-standing high cholesterol he attributes to genetics, seen a cardiologist and is on medication for it. A1C crossed into the pre-diabetic range for the first time; he used an over-the-counter continuous glucose monitor for three months and brought it back into range, no longer wearing it. Intermittent right knee pain with audible crunching on squats, wears a brace. Right elbow tendon pain assessed by an orthopaedic doctor who instructed him to continue training but use eccentric-tempo loading; resolved but recurs if stressed.

notable.note: A prospect who scored the offer 10 out of 10 before the price and was lost inside seven minutes of hearing it, with no payment plan offered at all — the only call in this batch where instalments were never raised. He is also the batch's most medically active prospect: three weeks into tirzepatide, on cardiologist-prescribed cholesterol medication, recently pre-diabetic, with a braced knee and an orthopaedic instruction to load his elbow eccentrically. Nobody asked whether a clinician had cleared ballistic kettlebell work, and the nutrition pillar pitched at him was a consolidated eating window, which sits directly against the protein-prioritisation his GLP-1 protocol requires. Two further items to verify centrally: the rep stated a specific performance guarantee (eight kilograms added to primary lifts or free continuation) that appears nowhere in the playbook, and the prospect twice called the rep 'Richard'.
